dining.name: JB's Smokehouse
dining.summary: The canyon-side smokehouse — brisket plates with Southwest Territory's scenery and shade.
description: JB's serves the chain smokehouse menu in the park's best-themed section, with a covered patio facing the canyon rockwork. It is the park's one planned-stop lunch.
The patio is the asset: shaded, scenic, and close enough to Raging Bull to watch the hyper run while eating.
tips: Claim patio shade before ordering on hot days.
App ordering skips the register queue on weekends.
dining.verdict: The best hot meal at the park in the best section to eat it. The barbecue is theme-park-grade but honest about it.

dining.name: County Fair Ice Cream Parlor
dining.priceNote: Sundaes and cones in the single-to-low teens
dining.summary: The old-fashioned parlor in the 1976 entrance section — sundaes, cones, and the park's best air conditioning.
description: The ice cream parlor in County Fair is the park's most charming food stop: a sit-down dessert counter in the historic entrance section, serving sundaes and cones with real tables and real climate control.
It doubles as the heat-recovery room. In July this is where families regenerate between the big coasters.
tips: The sundae is a two-person dessert; plan accordingly.
Mid-afternoon is the cool-off slot — the parlor empties after the lunch wave.
dining.verdict: A genuine parlor rather than a freezer case with a window. The sundae is the park's best dessert by a mile.
